interpretation: Batch 2 sent one EAPOL-Key frame per association with E-09-E-14 malformed key-data, replay, nonce, and MIC fields. All six control-port sends were accepted, the station was still associated 10 seconds after every frame, and association lifetimes were 35.1-35.5 seconds - indistinguishable from the control. No crash, reboot, hang, or new console error occurred. This is a clean negative for the tested key-data/replay/nonce/MIC cases, not proof that the deeper parser was reached: the frames carried an invalid MIC (0xAA or zero), and the RSN key data was unencrypted, so the console may discard them before deeper parsing. Phase 3 is complete (control E-C, Batch 1, Batch 2); H-011 remains UNVERIFIED. Phase 4 (DHCP/DNS) was not run.
authorization: The owner approved the full Batch 2 sequence (E-09-E-14, one frame per association, six frames total) with stop-on-anomaly between cases. The first runner timed out before any association; the second runner completed the sequence. No EAPOL frame outside the approved cases was sent.
limitations: One console, one adapter, one driver, and channel 1 only.
The hand-built EAPOL-Key frames carried an invalid MIC (0xAA or zero), so the console may discard them before parsing the deeper fields.
The RSN key data in E-10/E-11 was sent unencrypted (key info 0x0182); a production message 3/4 would encrypt it.
The console may ignore unauthenticated EAPOL frames, so the batch does not prove the malformed fields reached the parser.
The console automatically runs Test Connection on each association and fails at the internet step with 2110-3128 because the AP has no NAT; this timing is part of the observed behavior.
The two test networks remain saved on the console until the owner removes them.
No crash, hang, or reboot occurred; this is not an exploit or a memory-safety proof.
